title.en: Quadrilaterals: rectangles, rhombus, kite and trapezium

text.en: A carpenter has one 8 cm strip and wants to join it with another strip so that a thread through the ends forms a rectangle. How long must the other strip be, and where should they be joined?

A quadrilateral is a closed four-sided figure; the word comes from the Latin quadri for four and latus for side.
The four angles of any quadrilateral add up to 360°, because a diagonal splits it into two triangles of 180° each.
A rectangle is a quadrilateral with all angles 90° and opposite sides equal.
Using congruent triangles we can show that the diagonals of a rectangle are equal in length, so the carpenter's second strip is also 8 cm.
The diagonals of a rectangle also meet at their midpoints, so the strips must be joined in the middle of each.
A square is a rectangle with all four sides equal, so it keeps every property of a rectangle.
A rhombus has four equal sides; its diagonals bisect each other at right angles and also bisect the angles.
A parallelogram has opposite sides parallel and equal, opposite angles equal, and diagonals that bisect each other.
A kite has two pairs of equal adjacent sides, and its diagonals meet at right angles.
A trapezium has at least one pair of parallel sides, called its bases.

problem.en: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 80°, 95° and 100°. Find the fourth.

text.en: The four angles add up to 360°.

why.en: Angle sum property of a quadrilateral.
Subtract to find the missing angle.

prompt.en: Why must the second strip of the carpenter be 8 cm and meet the first at its midpoint?

requiredIdeas.en: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal.
So the strips cross at their midpoints.

commonMisconceptions.en: A square is not a rectangle.
The diagonals of a rectangle are unequal.

points.en: Angles of a quadrilateral add to 360°.
Rectangle diagonals are equal and bisect each other; rhombus diagonals meet at right angles.
Kite, trapezium and parallelogram differ in which sides are equal or parallel.
